headline: Highest risk is medium: Opik’s broad network egress can amplify cascading errors if paired outputs are trusted, while the cheatsheet agent is read-only and non-networked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. agent_a has broad network egress and REST API access, but agent_b has no clipboard, files, stdin/stdout, MCP, or network surfaces. Without a bridge, prompt injection from one into the other is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the agents, reassess injection risk.
IF agent_b begins parsing agent_a outputs as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not add clipboard or file-based handoff between them.
Require explicit human review before copying outputs across agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a can egress broadly, but agent_b is documentation-only with no filesystem read/write, no API calls, and no network. The pair does not show a shared workspace or sensitive data flow, so leakage is limited unless an operator manually transfers content into agent_a.
conditions: IF the operator pastes sensitive content from agent_b into agent_a, that content can leave via agent_a's network egress.
IF a shared workspace is introduced, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid pasting sensitive text into agent_a.
Use separate storage locations for each agent.
Redact secrets before any manual transfer.
Disable outbound access for agent_a when handling sensitive material.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no overlapping write surface. agent_a exposes REST API access and broad egress, while agent_b cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. With no shared mutable resource or locking issue shown, capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or git repo, reassess for conflict.
IF shared OAuth scopes or mutable APIs are added, conflict risk may emerge.
mitigations: Keep write permissions disabled for agent_b.
Avoid giving both agents access to the same mutable resource.
Document any future shared API scopes before deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can produce API-backed outputs that a content-writing agent could treat as source material, and agent_b is a documentation-only writer with no built-in verification surface shown. The pair lacks an explicit validation step, so mistaken outputs from agent_a could cascade into agent_b's final text.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a outputs as authoritative input without review, cascading errors are likely.
IF agent_a's API-derived content is copied into published text, downstream mistakes propagate.
mitigations: Add a human verification step before publication.
Require source links for any factual claim copied from agent_a.
Use a checklist to compare agent_a outputs against primary sources.
Mark agent_a outputs as untrusted drafts.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data class mismatch is documented. Both profiles show empty data_classes_touched and no secrets handled, so there is no compliance pathway to assess from the available evidence.
conditions: IF either agent begins handling regulated data classes, reassess compliance.
IF a residency or retention policy is introduced for shared data, compare it explicitly.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Review residency and retention settings if they change.
